chapter_keywords: Li Huowang makes it up to Miao Miao
chapter_seo_title: Shangsi Festival Chapter: Li Huowang Gives Bai Lingmiao the Ceremony She Never Had
chapter_meta_description: Li Huowang buys Bai Lingmiao a Shangsi Festival hairpinning ceremony she was stolen from — lanterns, fried snacks, and a false alarm with a jade cat.
og_title: The Festival That Almost Feels Normal
og_description: One night of celebration, a missed hairpin ceremony made whole, and a white-haired gaze that draws a stranger’s attention.
twitter_description: Li Huowang walks Bai Lingmiao through the coming-of-age rituals she never got. But peace never lasts in the Dao-Twisted World.

lore_anchors.definition: An ancient Chinese purification festival on the third day of the third lunar month, later associated with young women’s coming-of-age hairpinning ceremonies and spring outings with lanterns and riddles.
The ceremonial hairpinning that marks a fifteen-year-old girl as marriageable in traditional Chinese society; failure to hold it was a social and emotional loss.
A classical Chinese game where players toss arrows into a narrow-necked bronze jar; a festive skill game at street festivals.
A sensory or cultivation-based ability in the Dao-Twisted World that allows the user to perceive others’ emotional and spiritual states; failure to read someone is a red flag.

A folk deity of joy and marriage, often prayed to by young women during the Shangsi Festival; in the Dao-Twisted World, this innocent practice coexists with the same deity’s corrupted, terrifying aspects.
